subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class group authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but the feature changes Slack access-control semantics and the issue itself identifies Slack Connect/private shared-channel caveats.

options.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned normal routing, slash/action authorization, security audit docs, Slack Connect caveats, and tests while keeping existing defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

options.title: Reject private-channel boundary
options.body: Keep explicit channel ID allowlists as the only non-open Slack group authorization mode and document private/shared channels as insufficient for trust.

options.title: Defer to broader access-control design
options.body: Track the idea under a broader channel authorization redesign if maintainers want a cross-channel policy model rather than a Slack-specific value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned normal routing, slash/action authorization, security audit docs, Slack Connect caveats, and tests while keeping existing defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and the decision is security/product ownership rather than a mechanical code repair.
